correctness.rationale: For any polyhedral cone face the metric projector is locally its span projector. Complete exact rational enumeration of all 4096 triangle normal subsets bounds every such row sum by 8/5 (and all 8 subsets by 4/3 for three points). The positive input pair and explicit KKT multipliers prove sharpness for both real and positive input domains. Attached checker executed with all assertions passing.

evidence: Deza–Goldengorin–Pasechnik, arXiv:math/0306049 section 3.1.2: the four-point metric cone equals the cut cone and has seven cut rays and a large isometry group. It does not give the cross-norm Lipschitz constant of its nearest-point projection.
General Hilbert-space nonexpansiveness gives Euclidean contraction; switching to the six-dimensional maximum norm only yields a coarse factor bounded by sqrt(6), not the asserted 8/5.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Cone isometries, face combinatorics and Hilbert nonexpansiveness are genuinely broader geometric facts but do not mathematically dominate the exact edgewise sharp constant without additional face-projection computations.

value.rationale: The finite four-point metric cone is the first genuinely multi-triangle distance-restoration case. Sharp independent-entry error amplification controls robustness of repaired distances; it exceeds the single-triangle bound and is attained for positive measurement data. This motivated exact small-dimension invariant is not merely a recomputation of metric-cone rays or the optimization algorithm.
